To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the in-medium T matrices are dominated by attractive resonances, that the HQ transport coefficients increase with decreasing temperature, and that the resulting heavy-quark spectra are in good agreement with electron-decay data.

(1) the HQ drag coefficient increases with increasing temperature, (2) HQ transport coefficients are strongly enhanced at low temperatures due to resonant scattering, (3) a good description of the experimental heavy quark observables can be obtained within a strongly coupled QCD plasma, (4) HQ diffusion is dominated by elastic HQ scattering off light quark degrees of freedom, (5) HQ diffusion is not sensitive to the details of the interaction potential.
the drag coefficient of charm and bottom quarks increases with decreasing temperature and the heavy quark momentum diffusion coefficient increases with decreasing temperatures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the quark-guon plasma.
the investigation of the quark-glor plasma (QGP), which is a hot, dense medium created at RHIC.
the study of heavy-quark (Q) transport properties in the quark–gluon plasma (QCD) within a Bruckner many-body scheme.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the QGP is a strongly coupled system.
the QCD equation of state and the heavy quark diffusion coefficient are both consistent with a strongly coupled QCD plasma.
the QGP is strongly coupled.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the HQ diffusion is dominated by nonperturbative interactions in the QGP, which are not accounted for by perturbation theory, and that this nonperturbative interaction can be described by a Brueckener many-body scheme.
the nonperturbative approach is able to describe the experimental data, whereas the perturbative one fails to describe the data.
the heavy quark diffusion coefficient in QGP is not a small quantity and the perturbative QGP is not the correct starting point.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nonperturbative dynamics of the QGP is crucial for a quantitative description of heavy-quark transport.
nonperturbative QCD interactions can significantly enhance HQ diffusion coefficients in a QGP.
the HQ transport properties are sensitive to the nonperturbative dynamics of the QGP and can thus be used to constrain the QGP equation of state.
